items.title: Tinubu must intervene in Wike, APC govs’ feud — PCC
items.description: ***Says President has experience to resolve crisis lWike should explain Rainbow Coalition to APC govs —APC chieftain By Olasunkanmi Akoni & John Alechenu TO stop the prevailing face-off between governors elected on the platform of the All Progressives Congress, APC, and Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Minister, Nyesom Wike, from harming the ruling party at the 2027 elections, the APC Presidential Campaign Council, PCC, has urged President Bola Tinubu to intervene. Speaking on the issue, yesterday, APC PCC spokesman, Ima Niboro, who made the call, said the political dispute between the FCT Minister and the Progressive Governors Forum, PGF, over Wike’s cross-party initiative, the Rainbow Coalition, would be resolved internally soon. The governors are at daggers-drawn with Wike’s Rainbow Coalition that had fielded candidates from rival parties in many states, saying it would not only hurt APC candidates but also the re-election of President Tinubu Wike had described governors of the APC as “politically lazy”and accused prominent ones among them, including Kwara State governor, AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, and Governor Hope Uzodimma of Imo State, following their opposition to his Rainbow Coalition, ahead of the 2027 polls. The governors, led by their chairman Senator Hope Uzodimma, had earlier said they would not participate, support or endorse any alliance that could undermine President Tinubu’s re-election bid or affect APC candidates at any level. However, Wike, in an interview on Arise TV on Tuesday, dismissed the concerns, arguing that his decision to support Tinubu did not mean he had abandoned his political party or agreed that other parties should not field candidates. “They are politically lazy. When you have your local problems, don’t use Mr President as your excuse,” Wike, a kingmaker in the opposition Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, said. The minister maintained that the disagreements surrounding his political activities did not start with his decision to support Tinubu, recalling that he had faced opposition even when he was serving as governor of Rivers State and later as FCT minister. “This thing did not start today. It started at my appointment as a minister. They were not happy that I was Minister of FCT. Also, they were unhappy when I was governor,” he said. Wike said his knowledge of the political situation is greater than that of those criticising his activities, suggesting that his critics would understand his position better if they had access to the information available to him. “If they know what I know, they would not come out to shout,” he said. The former Rivers State governor also insisted that his support for Tinubu remains unchanged, arguing that supporting the President is separate from the activities of his political party. APC-PCC reacts Reacting to the exchange on Arise TV, yesterday, Niboro described the dispute as an internal disagreement between allies who share the same top-line goal and will be resolved internally. “I consider this a quarrel among political siblings. They are all working in the same direction, but there are differences in the details. Both camps agree that President Tinubu must return in 2027.” Addressing criticisms regarding Wike’s influence and the governors’ anxieties over state-level elections, Niboro urged APC leaders to cease public media battles and focus on grassroots campaigning. “If you’re a political leader, stop talking, go and work. Go and establish authority in your political base,” he urged. Despite concerns that the friction could fragment party structure ahead of the 2027 general elections, the PCC spokesman expressed confidence that the party’s machinery, particularly President Tinubu possesses the political experience required to reconcile the competing factions and manage the party’s expanding coalition. His words: “The ultimate beneficiary of this entire process is the President. The quarrel we are talking about is a quarrel that is trickling down to states and local government areas. But both camps agreed on re-electing the President. I do not see it as a direct challenge to the President himself, beyond the fact that he is a leader and it’s in his interest to intervene for peace. “If I were the President, for instance,you know, the President is an astute, very experienced politician, you cannot take that from him, I think he is networking these people. I know that. You see this kind of quarrel, you remember when we used to be in the PDP, sometimes the party gets so big, it becomes its own opposition. ‘’Those days, (Vincent Ogbulafor and) Ali Modu Sheriff used to say that PDP will rule for 60 years and there’s no opposition, but PDP itself became its opposition. “That’s how you had the breakaways from PDP and all those issues that led to the demise of PDP governance in this country. So, these are the issues that happen when you have big parties. It is inevitable. So, they have to be managed. ‘’These things have to be managed, and we have a leader who I think is competent enough to manage these things, and he will. Take my word.” Wike should meet APC governors, explain his Rainbow Coalition — APC chieftain Also reacting to the feud, a chieftain of APC, Mr. Joe Igbokwe, urged Wike to meet with the party’s governors and explain his proposed Rainbow Coalition aimed at mobilising support for President Tinubu’s re-election in 2027. Igbokwe said Wike remains an important political stakeholder whose influence could not simply be disregarded. “Wike is a critical stakeholder You can ignore him to your own peril. He has a command. He has followers,” Igbokwe said. However, he questioned the timing and approach of the Rainbow Coalition, saying Wike needed to consult the APC governors and explain his intentions to them. “Coming at this time, to put this (Rainbow Coalition) on the table, it’s not… he has to listen to the majority, sit down with the governors and explain,” he said. According to him, the disagreement should be resolved through conversations rather than public exchanges between the minister and the governors. “No man is an island. Explain to your colleagues what you are trying to do,” he added. Beware of pretentious govs, Osita urges Tinubu Igbokwe spoke as former Director-General of the Voice of Nigeria, VON, Osita Okechukwu, cautioned President Tinubu to be wary of some APC governors pushing him to dump Wike. He said yesterday in Abuja that the issue should have been handled within the party and not in the open. The former VON boss said: “In my 48 years in party politics, I have never seen where such an elementary issue was pretentiously thrown open. May I ask the governors: don’t you have access to Mr. President, and what is the proverbial caucus meant for? My summation is simple: Mr. President, beware of pretenders.” Okechukwu described those behind the call as “a few pretender governors, FPGs, ” who, according to him, have abandoned their people after using them. “To the best of my knowledge, some of these FPGs have wittingly or unwittingly used their electorate and recklessly abandoned them, and now want Mr. President to dump Wike,” he said. He further cautioned Tinubu not to fall into what he described as a booby trap linked to political inheritance in states where some governors had failed to deliver dividends of democracy. The APC chieftain argued that it would be wrong to dump Wike after benefitting from his political structure in 2023. He said: “Truly, it is improper for Mr. President to dump Wike after we harvested the Wike masquerade, which not only boosted our great party’s votes in 2023, but also denied Atiku Abubakar substantial votes, and will mobilise voters in states where the FPGs had alienated the electorate by personalising power.” On the claim by the progressives governors that they would lead Tinubu’s campaign, Okechukwu said the President had never sidelined them, adding that what he needed was extra votes. “Mr. President has never overlooked the governors. All he wants is supplementary votes from Wike, especially in states where the electorate is angry and where some of the FPGs have alienated the people. ‘’The governors should concentrate on strengthening their relationship with the electorate rather than asking Mr. President to abandon a political alliance that could broaden the APC’s electoral reach.” Okechukwu who is also a foundation member of the APC, urged the President to keep his options open and sustain a broad coalition ahead of 2027. items.title: Anambra debt controversy: Presidency dares Peter Obi to quit presidential race
items.description: By Bayo Wahab The Presidency has challenged Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate Peter Obi to honor his pledge to withdraw from the 2027 presidential race, after the Anambra State Government disputed his claim that he left the state without outstanding financial liabilities. Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, issued the challenge in a post on X on Wednesday, citing fresh claims by the Anambra State Government that Obi’s administration left behind unpaid loans and arrears. “Peter Obi claimed he left Anambra with a clean slate of debt,” Onanuga wrote, adding that the state government had since “confronted him with facts and figures” on Water Corporation workers, teachers, pensions and gratuities. He said Obi had also borrowed for “frivolous things” while in office, and asked whether the former governor would follow through on his earlier threat to withdraw from the presidential race. Peter Obi claimed he left Anambra with a clean slate of debt and even threatened to quit the presidential race if his claims were proven otherwise. Now, the Anambra government has confronted him with facts and figures showing he owed Water Corporation workers, teachers, and… pic.twitter.com/chyENjrKca — Bayo Onanuga, OON, CON (@aonanuga1956) September 16, 2026 The dispute began after the Anambra State Commissioner for Information and Value Reorientation, Dr Law Mefor, issued a statement disputing Obi’s claim that his administration left the state without outstanding liabilities. Mefor said Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s administration had cleared about N22 billion in gratuity arrears inherited from previous administrations, and owed to retired state and local government employees and teachers. He said Obi’s administration left outstanding loans, as well as arrears of salaries, pensions and gratuities, that subsequent administrations inherited. According to the state government, eight external loans linked to projects implemented during or inherited by the Obi administration remain outstanding, with a combined balance of $92.35 million, put at N127.37 billion as of June 30, 2026. The loans covered malaria control, erosion management, healthcare, education, community development and agricultural value-chain development. Mefor said the government would not be drawn into a debate over which administration paid particular arrears, but maintained that some legacy liabilities dating back to previous administrations remained outstanding. He cited salary arrears owed to workers of the defunct Water Corporation, which he said persisted throughout Obi’s tenure. Obi, had earlier claimed his administration cleared more than N35 billion in historical gratuities and arrears and left office without outstanding salary, pension or gratuity obligations. He also disputed the government’s claim about the ecological fund, saying more than N2.13 billion remained untouched in a First Bank account earmarked for the Oko/Umuchiana erosion crisis, in addition to over N75 billion in savings left behind by his administration. “If anybody can establish anything to the contrary, I will stop campaigning,” Obi said, challenging the state government or any other party to produce evidence contradicting his account. items.title: Amankwa-Manu demands stronger intelligence sharing among security agencies to fight drug trafficking
items.description: Former Deputy Defence Minister Kofi Amankwa-Manu is calling for stronger and more effective intelligence sharing among Ghana’s security agencies to tackle the growing threat of drug trafficking. He says the fight requires a coordinated national response, particularly as concerns continue to mount over major cocaine consignments linked to Ghana. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Wednesday, the former deputy ranking member of Parliament’s Defence and Interior Committee said Parliament must also play a stronger role in supporting government’s efforts. “This is a worrying, you know, thing which has to be tackled holistically. At tomorrow’s meeting, let me dare say that one thing I really want to see happen is the strengthening of the efficient and effective sharing of intelligence amongst, you know, all the security agencies, especially with regards to this fight against drug trafficking.” Mr Amankwa-Manu said training for security personnel was equally important, but stressed the need for agencies to stay ahead of criminal networks. “I agree with Dr Ishmael Norman on the issue of training and all that. That is very important. We need to do that, and we need to really be on top of and ahead of these criminals.” His call comes amid a series of major drug seizures linked to Ghana. French customs recently seized nearly 3.9 tonnes of cocaine concealed in a container of plastic waste that had departed Ghana. Ghanaian authorities have also intercepted large quantities of suspected cocaine, including 866 parcels at the Tema Harbour enclave in August and 192 compressed parcels in Wa this month. Against this backdrop, Mr Amankwa-Manu said he would seek Parliament’s leadership to consider recalling the House to deliberate on the matter. “From Parliament, especially from the opposition, what we can say is we have said. We’ve raised the issues, and in fact, I will want to approach the leadership of Parliament to really bring Parliament back for us to have an in-depth discussion in helping the government to fight this canker.” He said Parliament’s involvement could help develop a broader response involving its relevant committees. “If Parliament will have to come back to assist government in the fight against this canker, then we have to do.” Mr Amankwa-Manu said the Defence and Interior Committee and the Committee on Security and Intelligence could undertake detailed work before bringing their findings to the plenary. “We have committees. We have committees, and the Committee for Defence and Interior, and then the Committee on Security and Intelligence.” He added that the urgency of the situation required decisive action. “But after the committee has done its work, it has to come to plenary for others to also add their voices so that we can then send whatever we need to assist government in the fight against this canker, because it is getting out of hand, and the earlier something drastic and something major is done, the better it will be for the country.”

items.title: A Practical Guide to GameZone Promo Types
items.description: The GameZone promo page brings together several types of rewards, each designed around a different kind of platform activity. Instead of treating promotions as one standard bonus, GameZone separates them into daily offers, VIP benefits, verification incentives, tournament rewards, and limited-time campaigns. Some promotions are available as part of regular daily activity, while others depend on account status, scheduled events, or specific requirements. The listings can also change, particularly when GameZone introduces seasonal campaigns or concludes a temporary offer. Knowing the difference between each category can help you understand what you qualify for and when an offer is relevant. Limited Offers Give the GameZone Promo Page Variety GameZone's limited-time campaigns provide another reason to check its promotions regularly. Offers can be connected to holidays, anniversaries, platform milestones, giveaways, or other special events. Their defining feature is the fixed period in which they operate. A limited campaign can disappear once its scheduled period ends. Missing one, therefore, does not necessarily affect other promotions on your account. A quick look at the current listings can tell you whether GameZone is running something outside its regular offers. It is also important to look beyond the headline reward. Temporary campaigns can have specific participation dates, eligibility requirements, or other conditions that determine whether you can actually receive the advertised benefit. Daily GameZone Promo Rewards for Regular Players One of the simpler ways to use GameZone promotions is through its daily free-entry offers. The Free Win promotion provides two free entries each day for both Tongits Plus and Poker Plus . Players can therefore join selected activities without using credits for those entries. The promotion also covers the Pro Cup Tournament , giving players opportunities to participate in scheduled competitions throughout the day. As of September 2, 2026 , the listed Pro Cup times were 12:15 PM, 6 PM, 7 PM, 8 PM, and 11 PM . These schedules can change, so players should check the current listing before planning around a particular tournament. You do not need to reorganize your entire playing routine around it. Instead, the free entries can fit naturally into a normal session. Check the current promotion details to see which games, entries, and schedules are covered before participating. Building Benefits Through VIP Levels GameZone also has promotions connected to account progression. Its VIP system increases a player's level automatically through continued activity, with higher levels potentially providing additional benefits. They can include improved GameZone rebate rates, access to exclusive events, and other offers associated with higher VIP tiers. Rather than requiring players to manually purchase or apply for a particular status, the system connects progression with activity on the platform. Their value becomes more relevant to regular users who continue playing over a longer period. A rebate, for example, can return a portion of eligible activity according to the applicable promotion rules. However, the exact benefit depends on the terms attached to your account level and the specific offer. If you are already using GameZone consistently, checking your current VIP status can give you a better idea of which benefits are available to you. It also helps you distinguish between rewards you already qualify for and promotions that require different conditions. Verification Unlocks Even More GameZone Promo Offers Not every GameZone promo requires gameplay. Some offers are connected to account verification, including the platform's Know Your Customer (KYC) process. KYC is a standard verification procedure used to establish an account holder's identity. On GameZone, completing the required verification steps can make eligible players entitled to free points and other smaller incentives tied to the promotion. The important distinction is that verification serves a practical purpose beyond receiving a reward. Properly establishing an account helps the platform meet its security and compliance requirements while giving users access to account features that may depend on completed verification. For this reason, players should not approach a KYC-related promotion as simply another bonus. The underlying account requirement matters just as much as the incentive attached to it. Tournament and Newcomer Promos Change Occasionally Some promotional categories are more dependent on GameZone's current schedule. Newcomer and tournament offers fall into this group, meaning their availability can change as campaigns begin and end. Newcomer promotions are aimed at people who are just starting on the platform. Depending on the campaign, an introductory offer may include rebates based on an initial deposit or other account activity. However, as of September 2, 2026, no newcomer promotion was listed as currently available. Tournament promotions have a different audience. They can support competitions involving Tongits , poker, and other multiplayer formats through additional prize pools, bonus entries, or leaderboard-related incentives. Neither category should be treated as permanently available. A player who sees an older announcement may assume that the same reward still exists, even after its campaign has ended. The safest approach is to check the current promotion page before making plans around a newcomer or tournament offer. Look at the dates, eligibility rules, and participation requirements rather than relying solely on the name of the promotion. Use the GameZone Promo Page as Your Reference GameZone's promotional system makes more sense when each offer is viewed according to what it is designed to do. Daily free entries can suit regular players, VIP benefits reward continued platform activity, and KYC incentives are tied to account verification. Tournament campaigns appeal more to competitive users, while newcomer and limited-time offers depend heavily on what GameZone is running at a particular moment. A reward available to VIP users may not apply to a new account, while a tournament offer may only matter during a specific event. The terms determine what you can actually receive. If you care to explore the latest GameZone promo offers, the promotion page is the most useful place to start. FAQs Q: What is a GameZone rebate? A: A rebate returns a portion of eligible activity as a reward, according to the promotion's terms. Q: How do I increase my VIP level? A: Your VIP level increases automatically based on your activity on the platform. Q: What is KYC? A: KYC, or Know Your Customer, is the identity-verification process used to establish your account. Q: What is needed for KYC? A: KYC requires an active mobile phone number and a valid Philippine government-issued ID to proceed. Q: What payment methods can I use on GameZone? A: Supported options include GCash, GrabPay, Maya, and QR PH-supported payment services. L’article A Practical Guide to GameZone Promo Types est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: African elephant Madhubala on ‘antibiotics’ after collapsing at Karachi’s Safari Park
items.description: KARACHI: Despite carrying out several tests, including an X-ray, over the past two days, the authorities in Safari Park remain clueless about what caused the sudden collapse of African elephant Madhubala in her enclosure, it emerged on Wednesday. Responding to queries, a spokesperson for the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) said that Madhubala suffered from “acute weakness and low immunity levels” following prolonged treatment for tuberculosis and that’s what caused her sudden fall. “While all her laboratory tests are just fine, she is being given antibiotics as a precautionary measure on the advice of a senior local vet. No fracture has been detected in the X-ray,” KMC spokesperson Daniyal Alishan Siyal told Dawn , adding that all medical reports were emailed to Sri Lankan wildlife health specialist Dr Buddhika for final assessment. When asked why she is being given antibiotics when no bacterial infection has been detected, he said, “I am told that she has elevated infection markers, though no specific cause has been detected.” The African elephant is suffering from ‘acute weakness and low immunity levels’ Madhubala, he pointed out, could now stand on her feet and the supporting crate belt had been removed. On the swelling on her right hind thigh, he claimed that, “It was caused by her fall.” He rejected the information that Madhubala was acutely dehydrated on the day of her fall because there wasn’t sufficient water to keep her cool on hot days. “There were no power breakdowns that could lead to water issues,” Mr Siyal said. Foot abscess recovery? Safari Park Director Amjad Zaidi two days ago stated that it’s apparently the swelling on her right thigh, which was preventing her from using her leg. He had also stated that Madhubala had “recovered” from a foot infection. Sources stated Madhubala’s swelling on her right hind thigh might be indicating spread of abscess from the foot (on the same affected leg) that she had been fighting for some period. “Elevated infection markers mean her body’s immune system is reacting to a problem, though her test results cannot tell the exact cause,” a senior vet shared. Steady signs of improvement: KMC The KMC released a press statement on Madhubala’s condition, stating that the elephant is showing steady signs of improvement and continues to receive round-the-clock veterinary care and close medical monitoring. “The latest health assessments have revealed several encouraging signs of improvement. Madhubala is now able to stand independently without harness support, marking a positive development in her recovery. Her vital parameters remain stable, while she continues to maintain a good appetite and remains alert and responsive,” it says. It further adds that Madhubala is undergoing daily health assessments and blood tests, while X-rays of her hind quarters are also being conducted regularly. “These diagnostic procedures are being carried out with the support of the Sindh Institute of Animal Health, enabling veterinary experts to closely monitor her physical condition and evaluate her progress. “Madhubala’s dedicated keeper team remains with her around the clock. The keepers, who have been closely involved in her daily care, are working in close coordination with the veterinary team to ensure that she receives appropriate nutrition, care, supervision and support throughout her recovery,” it adds. Madhubala had been in solitary confinement at Karachi Zoo following the tragic death of her companion Noor Jehan who died in 2023 after a tragic fall in her enclosure. Noor Jehan’s autopsy report released by the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) showed that she died from a severe blood parasitic infection and internal trauma combined with a lack of proper medical care. Left alone at the zoo, Madhubala was successfully relocated to Safari Park where she was reunited with her sisters, Sonia and Malika, in November 2024, under the supervision of Four Paws — an international animal welfare organisation that worked extensively with the KMC for elephant care. The success story of her reunion faded soon as Sonia died a month later after collapsing in her Safari enclosure. Lab reports later showed that she suffered from multiple chronic illnesses, affecting almost all vital organs, indicating prolonged neglect in her care and failure in timely diagnosis. Successive deaths of captive elephants raised public outcry, forcing the KMC to set up an 18-member body to look after Madhubala and Malika, both of whom were diagnosed with tuberculosis. The four female elephants were brought to Karachi from Tanzania in 2010 at a very young age under a controversial arrangement. Published in Dawn, September 17th, 2026

items.title: Indian transgender patients left in limbo following legal amendments
items.description: When transgender woman Kali Sidharth Medepalli began hormone replacement therapy in India, she expected to complete her medical transition and undergo surgery within a year. But just months after she began treatment earlier this year, India’s parliament amended the country’s transgender law, and the clinic where she was receiving care stopped her medicines. “Everything shut down,” the 23-year-old communications specialist and LGBTQ rights activist said in the southern city of Hyderabad. Kali...

items.title: US again denies Palestinian leader Abbas visa to attend UN assembly
items.description: The United States has denied Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas an entry visa to attend the UN General Assembly in New York next week, a source familiar with the case said Wednesday. In a separate statement that did not mention Abbas by name, the State Department say it would deny visas to members of the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) and officials with the Palestinian Authority (PA), "as a consequence of their failure to reform, contrary to their commitments to the United States, and their ongoing activities that undermine the prospects for peace."

items.title: Feijóo se enroca con Vox y cierra la puerta a que ningún menor de Ceuta vaya a la Península
items.description: El PP y la justicia estrechan el ya limitado margen de maniobra del Gobierno para resolver la crisis de Ceuta. Mientras la Audiencia Nacional paraliza de manera cautelar la utilización del puerto para acoger a inmigrantes en plenos preparativos para trasladar allí a casi 2000 de ellos para aliviar el problema en las playas de Ceuta, la dirección del PP dejó este miércoles clarísimo que cierra por completo la puerta a que ningún menor sea trasladado a la Península siquiera temporalmente, mientras se resuelven sus expedientes y se los 0intenta devolver a Marruecos. Los populares se alinean con Vox en el rechazo a los traslados de menores, como evidenció además su voto a favor este martes en el Congreso a una iniciativa de la extrema derecha que se opone al realojo de los niños y jóvenes. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La jueza busca quién coordinó, financió y decidió el operativo de la entrada masiva a Ceuta en Marruecos
items.description: El objetivo es claro: identificar a los promotores y coordinadores del gran salto a Ceuta el pasado 30 y 31 de julio. La movilización masiva de “entre 75.000 y 85.000 personas”, dice la jueza María Tardón, “difícilmente puede producirse sin recursos materiales y financieros”. Por eso, la magistrada de la Audiencia Nacional quiere esclarecer cómo miles de personas pudieron enterarse en un periodo corto de tiempo de que se estaba gestando un paso fronterizo y cómo pudieron transportarse todas hasta la zona marroquí de Fnideq-Castillejos desde distintos puntos de Marruecos. La instructora da veracidad a los indicios policiales que apuntaban a que pudo haber “agentes dinamizadores” en la frontera que supuestamente guiaron a los migrantes y ha pedido tanto a la Policía como al Centro Nacional de Inteligencia (CNI) que ayuden en la identificación de estas personas, consultando para ello bases de datos internacionales. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Así podría secuestrar internet un enjambre de agentes de IA: “Tardaríamos unos añitos en arreglarlo todo”
items.description: En estos días de debate sobre la capacidad de destrucción de la inteligencia artificial (IA), falta siempre desarrollar un detalle: ¿cómo lo haría exactamente? ¿Qué podría pasar en concreto? No hay tantas respuestas específicas. Pero el propio Dario Amodei, presidente ejecutivo de Anthropic, mencionó una opción en su controvertida propuesta para ralentizar el desarrollo de la IA . Amodei se planteaba algo que, según sus palabras, puede pasar dentro de seis o doce meses: ¿qué pasaría si un enjambre de IA es capaz de “tomar el control de todo internet”? Seguir leyendo

items.title: Beck, músico: “En los noventa hubo mucha testosterona. Cuando tocaba una balada, me tiraban botellas llenas de orina”
items.description: Es su quinta jornada promocional seguida y acusa cierto cansancio, o tal vez ese desapego tan cool forme parte de su carácter. La duda aparece al estrechar la mano de Beck Hansen (Los Ángeles, 56 años) en la sede parisina de su discográfica, pegada al restaurante donde trabaja el chef guapo de Emily in Paris . En el exterior, una legión de turistas dispara sus móviles como metralletas. Parecen bastante más interesados en el toldo rojo del establecimiento que en el hombre menudo y de edad imprecisa que acaba de entrar en el edificio, al que nadie reconoce pese a que, en una época no tan lejana, fue una de las figuras esenciales de lo que entonces se llamó música alternativa. Se acerca a los sesenta, pero de lejos parecería un veinteañero, con su camisa negra de corte vaquero y zapatos de dandi decadente, al estilo de su venerado Serge Gainsbourg , que dibujan una silueta de hilos de alambre que siempre resultó un tanto improbable para una estrella del rock. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Juan José Tamayo, teólogo: “Jesús de Nazaret fue una persona vulnerable, frágil, para nada un héroe, más bien un fracasado”
items.description: Enero de 2006. El Nobel de Literatura José Saramago y el teólogo Juan José Tamayo salen juntos del Hotel Los Seises. A las nueve en punto pasan delante de la Giralda y empiezan a repicar las campanas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ‘La bola negra’ entra en la carrera de los Oscar con una expectación insólita y la campaña más grande de la historia del cine español
items.description: Nunca una película española ha encarado la temporada de premios cinematográficos internacionales desde una posición tan privilegiada como La bola negra, que la Academia de Cine anunció ayer, miércoles, que representará a España en los Oscar en la categoría de mejor película internacional. Solo La sociedad de la nieve, de Juan Antonio Bayona, y Sirât, de Oliver Laxe, que en la pasada edición de los galardones de Hollywood logró dos nominaciones, se acercaron a este fenómeno. El público que la ha visto en festivales la idolatra; casi toda la crítica la ama. Y en Norteamérica va a contar con el respaldo económico en su lanzamiento de la todopoderosa plataforma Netflix. Si Laxe pasó semanas en Estados Unidos apoyando su filme, Javier Calvo y Javier Ambrossi, los Javis, los directores de La bola negra , no se van a quedar atrás. “Por nosotros que no quede”, confesaron ayer a la prensa española. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El último servicio de Pedro Sánchez
items.description: Las quinielas sobre cuándo convocará Pedro Sánchez las elecciones generales han comenzado . El presidente del Gobierno dice querer alargar la legislatura hasta el final , pero seguramente aprovechará cuando vea una mejor oportunidad política. Y, sin embargo, Sánchez no tendrá ningún mal resultado en los comicios de 2027, sino al contrario. Su último servicio a España será enviar a la oposición a un PSOE hegemónico, ya fulminados los partidos del 15-M. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La IA, las lágrimas de Strogatz y el momento Kaspárov
items.description: Steven Strogatz es uno de los matemáticos más populares del mundo por sus investigaciones sobre sincronización, biología y redes complejas, pero también por la claridad con la que divulga su disciplina. ¿Alguna vez ha dicho “qué pequeño es el mundo”? Fueron él y Duncan Watts quienes explicaron a finales de los noventa por qué siempre hay alguien que conoce a alguien que conoce a otra persona que. Pues bien, Strogatz —un caballero educado en Princeton y Harvard , profesor de Cornell, miembro de la Academia de Ciencias estadounidense, citadísimo autor— se echó a llorar la semana pasada durante una entrevista. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Von der Leyen anuncia un plan de seguridad para Europa sin Estados Unidos
items.description: La presidenta de la Comisión Europea, Ursula von der Leyen, no mencionó ni una sola vez a Estados Unidos en las 22 páginas del discurso que pronunció ayer en el Parlamento Europeo, desgranado durante cerca de 75 minutos . Toda una maniobra de resistencia discursiva —como diría Michel Foucault — frente a Donald Trump, el tsunami que tambalea con sus mensajes y sus anuncios el tablero geopolítico global, el líder que está haciendo que Europa se mueva para desplegar un marco de seguridad a golpe de amenazar con la retirada estadounidense. En su discurso sobre el estado de la Unión en Estrasburgo, la presidenta de la Comisión Europea dibujó un mecanismo de seguridad sin Washington para los países miembros y otros aliados de la UE, para los que EE UU ha sido un protector clave desde el final de la II Guerra Mundial. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los rectores quieren reforzar los controles antes de mandar alumnos a México tras el asesinato de Claudia Tacoronte
items.description: Las universidades españolas revisarán sus controles antes de mandar alumnos a México tras el asesinato el pasado sábado de la estudiante de la Universidad de Granada (UGR), Claudia Tacoronte , que estaba de intercambio en la Universidad Autónoma del Estado de Morelos (UAEM) en el centro del país. “Habrá que revisar y reforzar las pautas que se trasladan a los estudiantes”, explica a EL PAÍS un portavoz de la conferencia de rectores (CRUE), que engloba 77 universidades del centenar que hay en España. items.title: “Exceso de confianza” y control financiero laxo, las claves del agujero dejado por el exatleta olímpico Carlos Sala
items.description: El agujero de 150.000 euros que presuntamente dejó el exatleta olímpico Carlos Sala en su gestión como responsable de una entidad que promueve el deporte escolar fue descubierto demasiado tarde, cuando el daño ya estaba hecho y el Consell Esportiu del Barcelonès Nord (Cebnord) había entrado en situación “crítica”. El órgano, que se nutre sobre todo de subvenciones públicas, trata de mantenerse a flote para garantizar la actividad deportiva en las escuelas de Badalona, Santa Coloma y Sant Adrià, al tiempo que debate sobre si se podría haber evitado el desfalco y de qué manera. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Blanca Castro, la primera vecina que se enfrenta a una histórica familia de rentistas con todo su vecindario detrás
items.description: La familia Campos Cebrián-González Ruano no estuvo en la sala. Los vecinos del número 22 de la calle General Lacy esperaban con ansia a los Campos Cebrián-González Ruano porque, aunque estos llevan siendo sus rentistas desde hace más de 80 años, todavía no les ponen cara. Ni Blanca Castro, ni Santiago Sanz, ni Jacqueline Leca, ni María Gutiérrez conocen el tono de voz de sus rentitas. Si se cruzaran por la calle, no podrían reconocerse. Ninguno sabe si son altos o son bajos, rubios o morenos, si son de los que ganan en las distancias cortas o en cambio parecen tan fríos como los burofaxes que fueron llegando, uno por uno, a los 32 vecinos del edificio para notificarles —con cuatro meses de antelación— que sus vidas “terminan a todos los efectos” una vez finalicen sus contratos de arrendamiento. Por eso en los pasillos del Juzgado de Primera Instancia número 82 de Madrid había cierto cuchicheo en la mañana del miércoles entre los vecinos que acompañaron a Blanca, la primera de las demandas por la familia Campos Cebrián-González Ruano por “expiración de contrato”. “¿Son ellos?”, se preguntaban mirando de reojo a los presentes. No. No eran ellos. Habían enviado a sus abogados. Ninguno ha querido hablar con este periódico. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La crisis de la vivienda y el avance de la extrema derecha marcan las elecciones regionales en Berlín
items.description: La lucha contra la escasez de vivienda puede llevar al partido La Izquierda, por primera vez en la historia, a liderar el Gobierno regional de Berlín tras las elecciones del próximo domingo. Su candidata, Elif Eralp, podría convertirse en la primera alcaldesa germano-turca de la capital. Pero nunca antes, unas elecciones habían estado tan reñidas. La Izquierda y los conservadores —actualmente en el Gobierno— están casi igualados en los sondeos, seguidos de cerca por el partido de extrema derecha Alternativa para Alemania (AfD) —que duplicaría su apoyo— y el de Los Verdes. items.title: Del veto de Mamdani al entusiasmo en Estonia: las escuelas del mundo afrontan el uso de la IA
items.description: Sandra Martinez Roe, una madre de Los Ángeles, espera que su hijo nunca utilice la inteligencia artificial en el colegio. “No voy a permitir que mis niños sean unos conejillos de Indias”, afirma por teléfono. La junta escolar de la ciudad le concedió su deseo, al menos temporalmente, hace dos semanas. El Distrito Escolar Unificado de Los Ángeles (LAUSD, por sus siglas en inglés) ha expulsado a la IA de las aulas públicas este curso. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Mucho más que el ex de Madonna: Guy Ritchie dirige un imperio criminal británico en las series
items.description: Para muchos, Guy Ritchie nunca dejará de ser el exmarido de Madonna . Pero este director británico de pura cepa es mucho más que aquella relación tan publicitada que terminó en 2008 con una batalla por la custodia de sus hijos y un divorcio millonario. Ritchie es, de hecho, a sus 57 años, uno de los niños bonitos de la industria del streaming . Este mismo septiembre, y pese a que la taquilla de cine se resista hoy a su inconfundible estilo, lanza dos series muy populares en plataformas, además de su película anual en salas . Seguir leyendo

Recetas virales de aperitivos: ¿ideas originales o crímenes gastronómicos?
items.description: Hemos probado porras fit , tiramisús para gymbros , cheesecakes japoneses , helados de tres ingredientes , panes sin hidratos o ensaladas de TikTok , y contra todo pronóstico, seguimos vivas. Así que, ¿por qué no seguir con El Comidistest , esa peligrosa sección en la que sometemos a examen las recetas que lo petan en las redes? No vamos a negar el sufrimiento de ingerir determinados engendros, pero de vez en cuando también descubrimos ideas que están realmente bien. Y siempre, siempre, siempre nos reímos de las tontadas de los influencers , que es de lo que se trata. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Cinco ciudades en España para comer muy bien más allá de Madrid y Barcelona
items.description: Durante años, para comer muy bien en una ciudad de España parecía que se tenía que escoger entre Madrid y Barcelona . Después llegaron San Sebastián , Bilbao , Valencia o Sevilla para demostrar que el mapa gastronómico es mucho más grande. Ahora la revolución sucede un poco más lejos de las ciudades más visitadas del país: en enclaves donde la cocina se ha convertido en una razón para un viaje por derecho propio. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El mapa físico para viajar por carretera aún compite con el GPS (al menos en los Países Bajos)
items.description: Los mapas de carreteras modernos surgieron en el siglo XX, aupados por la aparición del automóvil, patentado en enero de 1886 por el ingeniero e inventor alemán Carl Benz. La primera en imprimirlos a escala nacional, en 1904, fue la editorial estadounidense Rand McNally. En 1910, los hermanos franceses André y Édouard Michelin, fundadores de la conocida firma de neumáticos, crearon en Europa la famosa guía y produjeron luego unos documentos de rutas que han ido evolucionando en otros lugares. En la actualidad, estas representaciones cartográficas de redes principales y locales incluyen información sobre peajes, señalización, zonas de descanso y hasta atracciones turísticas. Más de un siglo después, la clásica versión en papel aguanta el tirón de los navegadores digitales: en los Países Bajos, la Real Asociación Neerlandesa de Turismo ANWB ofrece dos millones de ejemplares gratuitos a sus cinco millones de socios —en un país de 18 millones de personas—. Seguir leyendo

items.title: It is getting out of hand – Amankwa-Manu wants Parliament recalled over drug trafficking
items.description: Former Deputy Defence Minister Kofi Amankwa-Manu is calling for the recall of Parliament to enable lawmakers to hold an in-depth discussion on Ghana’s growing drug trafficking concerns. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Wednesday, the former deputy ranking member of the Defence and Interior Committee of Parliament said the problem requires a coordinated national response. He said Parliament must play a role in helping government confront the threat, particularly through its committees on Defence and Interior, and Security and Intelligence. “This is a worrying, you know, thing which has to be tackled holistically,” he said. “At tomorrow’s meeting, let me dare say that one thing I really want to see happen is the strengthening of the efficient and effective, you know, sharing of intelligence amongst, you know, all the security agencies, especially with regards to this fight against drug trafficking.” Mr Amankwa-Manu said Parliament could also contribute through stronger oversight and collaboration with the security agencies. “I will want to approach the leadership of Parliament to really bring Parliament back for us to have an in-depth discussion in helping the government to fight this canker,” he said. Asked directly whether he wanted Parliament recalled over the matter, he responded: “Yes, I want to recall.” “If we can have a recall just to appoint a few people, this is an issue affecting the image and the country as a whole, and it is important that we all put our shoulders to the wheel to find a solution to this problem,” he said. His call comes amid a series of major drug-related cases involving Ghana in recent months. In August, the Tema Regional Police Command intercepted 866 parcels of suspected cocaine concealed in sacks of gari, with an estimated street value of US$6.9 million. Three people were arrested in that operation. In June, NACOC also began investigations into the seizure in Australia of about 320 kilogrammes of methamphetamine allegedly shipped from Ghana. More recently, French Customs seized nearly 3.9 tonnes of cocaine from a container that had arrived from Ghana. NACOC subsequently arrested three suspects in Ghana on allegations of links to the network. On Wednesday, two suspects were also remanded in Wa after 192 compressed wraps of cocaine were intercepted following an intelligence-led operation. Against this backdrop, Mr Amankwa-Manu said Parliament must consider what more it can do. “We have committees. We have committees, and the Committee for Defence and Interior, and then the Committee on Security and Intelligence,” he said. He explained that the committees could first examine the issue before taking their findings to the full House. “But after the committee is done its work, it has to come to plenary for others to also add their voices so that we can then, you know, send whatever we need to assist government in the fight against this canker,” he said. Mr Amankwa-Manu stressed the urgency of the situation. “Because it is getting out of hand, and the earlier something drastic and something major is done, the better it will be for the country.”

items.title: IAEA safeguards deal for Chashma-5 nuclear power plant secured
items.description: • 1,200MW reactor’s dome placed early; commissioning set for 2028 • Talks held with China on N-cooperation ISLAMABAD: The Inte­rnational Atomic Energy Agency and Pakistan on Wednesday signed a safeguards agreement for the 1,200-megawatt Chashma-5 nuclear power plant to bolster the country’s energy security while ensuring international non-proliferation standards. IAEA Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi and Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission Chairman Raja Ali Raza Anwar signed the pact at the agency’s headquarters in Vienna. The signing took place on the sidelines of the 70th IAEA General Conference. Shan Zhongde, chairman of the China Atomic Energy Authority, witnessed the ceremony. The agreement, which governs the application of safeguards at Unit-5 of the Chashma plant, was unanimously approved by the IAEA Board of Governors in March. According to a statement on the signing, the agreement marks a critical step toward implementing safeguards for the new facility. Officials noted that it reflects the international community’s continued confidence in Pakistan’s commitment to the peaceful use of nuclear energy and its adherence to global non-proliferation obligations. Construction of the Chashma-5 (C-5) facility is progressing rapidly, with early completion of the reactor’s dome placement among its recent milestones. Scheduled for commissioning in 2028, the unit is expected to add a substantial source of low-carbon, low-cost electricity to Pakistan’s national grid to support climate objectives and sustainable economic growth. Pakistan currently operates six nuclear power plants with a combined installed capacity of 3,530 megawatts. According to the Atomic Energy Commission, these plants have maintained an average capacity factor exceeding 90pc. Officials highlighted that the country possesses more than 100 reactor-years of operational experience, maintaining a strong record of safe, secure and safeguarded operations under international standards. Prior to the signing ceremony, Pakistani and Chinese delegations met to discuss ongoing and future cooperation in the peaceful applications of nuclear science and technology. Anwar led the Pakistani delegation, while Zhongde headed the Chinese group. Mohammad Kamran Akhtar Malik, Pakistan’s ambassador to Austria and permanent representative to the IAEA, also participated in the bilateral discussions. Published in Dawn, September 17th, 2026

items.title: Le Canada et l'Allemagne s'allient pour une IA "au service de l'humain"
items.description: Le Canada et l'Allemagne ont annoncé travailler ensemble au développement d'une intelligence artificielle « au service de l'humain » face aux inquiétudes croissantes sur les risques pour l'humanité des modèles les plus avancés. « Aucun pays ne peut construire seul. C'est pourquoi le Canada et l'Allemagne lancent une alliance » afin « de construire une (IA éthique), avec nos valeurs », a déclaré le ministre canadien de l'Intelligence artificielle, Evan Solomon, lors de la conférence ALL IN, dédiée à l'IA, à Montréal. « Le Canada et l'Allemagne s'engagent sur la base de la démocratie, des valeurs » pour « transformer la recherche en produits (d'IA) fiable », a ajouté le ministre allemand du Numérique, Karsten Wildberger. C'est un « moment décisif » pour le développement de l'IA, et Berlin et Ottawa souhaitent soutenir une « technologie au service de l'humain » , a poursuivi Evan Solomon. Le débat sur les risques de l'IA est monté en puissance depuis le début de l'été après une série d'incidents et de déclarations apocalyptiques de plusieurs professionnels du secteur. Dans le cadre de leur partenariat, les deux pays se sont notamment engagés à financer l'organisation canadienne à but non lucratif LoiZéro, fondée par le professeur Yoshua Bengio qui est considéré comme l'un des pères de l'IA, à hauteur de 300 millions de dollars canadiens (187 millions d'euros). Ce financement doit « propulser la prochaine phase de recherche » de l'organisation sur des systèmes d'IA sûrs et éthiques et lui permettre d' « étendre ses activités en Europe », notamment en ouvrant un bureau à Berlin, a annoncé la startup de Yoshua Bengio, lauréat en 2018 du prix Turing, l'équivalent du Nobel pour l'informatique, avec Geoffrey Hinton et Yann LeCun. Dans un entretien accordé à l'AFP, M. Bengio a jugé que l'humanité était en train de perdre le contrôle de cette technologie et a appelé à la mise en place de « garde-fous » face à un « enjeu international ». Cette alliance entre Berlin et Ottawa est un exemple supplémentaire du rapprochement opéré entre le Canada et les pays européens. La présidente de la Commission européenne, Ursula von der Leyen, a proposé mercredi que le Canada puisse devenir le premier pays « membre associé » de l'UE, devant son Premier ministre Mark Carney, longuement applaudi par les eurodéputés. items.title: Gold rises over 1% as investors digest Fed hike, oil rally stalls
items.description: Gold prices rose more than 1% on Thursday ‌as investors digested the U.S. Federal Reserve’s interest rate hike and its signal that further policy tightening may follow, while an earlier rally in oil prices lost momentum. Spot gold was up 1.1% at $4,310.49 per ​ounce, as of 0149 GMT, after hitting a near six-week low on Wednesday. U.S. gold futures for ​December delivery were down roughly 1% at $4,348.70. Oil prices fell, extending losses from the previous session, as reports that Saudi Arabia is offering additional crude cargoes through Oman eased fears of supply disruptions. “Oil prices remain a key factor to watch. If oil prices continue to decline, that could support higher gold prices, at least from a medium-term perspective. Until that materialises, I expect gold to remain range-bound,” said Kelvin Wong, senior market analyst at OANDA. The current uptick in gold is also largely driven by technical factors, with the Fed’s hawkish message already priced into the market, he added. Although gold is considered an inflation hedge, higher ‌rates ⁠reduce its appeal by boosting the attractiveness of interest-bearing assets. The Fed raised interest rates on Wednesday and flagged more hikes in the coming months, with new U.S. central bank chief Kevin Warsh joining a unanimous decision that effectively acknowledges the Trump administration’s inability so ​far to control ​inflation that policymakers worry ⁠could worsen. Updated quarterly economic projections showed 16 of 18 policymakers anticipate at least one more quarter-percentage-point hike by the end of ​this year, with only two of them seeing rates remaining stable ​from here. The Bank ⁠of England looks set to keep rates on hold on Thursday but investors are watching for any hint that higher energy prices could force it to follow the Fed’s ⁠example. In the ​Middle East, Saudi warplanes pounded Yemen, the Houthis said, ​as the Iran-backed fighters solidified their gains after a lightning advance. Spot silver rose 1.4% at $63.83, platinum firmed 1.6% to $1,780.55 ​and palladium climbed 2% to $1,295.00.

items.title: Womey/N’Zérékoré : douze ans après, retour sur le drame qui a coûté la vie à huit membres d’une mission Ebola
items.description: Douze ans après les événements, le nom de Womey reste associé à l’un des épisodes les plus tragiques de l’épidémie d’Ebola en Guinée. Le 16 septembre 2014, une mission de sensibilisation dépêchée dans cette localité de la préfecture de N’Zérékoré a été prise à partie par des habitants. Huit personnes ont été tuées, dont trois professionnels des médias. À l’époque, la Guinée forestière était confrontée à une forte propagation du virus Ebola. La peur, les rumeurs et la méfiance envers les équipes sanitaires compliquaient les opérations de sensibilisation. C’est dans ce contexte qu’une délégation s’est rendue à Womey pour expliquer aux populations les risques liés à la maladie et les moyens de prévention. Selon les informations rapportées à l’époque, la mission avait d’abord été accueillie normalement avant que la situation ne dégénère. Des habitants auraient lancé des pierres contre les membres de la délégation. Certains ont réussi à fuir, tandis que d’autres ont été rattrapés. Les corps de huit victimes ont ensuite été retrouvés dans une fosse septique à Womey. Huit victimes Les victimes étaient issues des secteurs de la santé, de l’administration, de la religion et des médias. Parmi elles figuraient Facely Camara, reporter stagiaire à Liberté FM, Molou Chérif, technicien à Radio Rurale de N’Zérékoré, et Sidiki Sidibé, technicien stagiaire dans la même radio. Le Comité pour la protection des journalistes (CPJ) a documenté leur mort comme liée à leur présence sur le terrain pour couvrir une campagne de sensibilisation contre Ebola. Les cinq autres victimes étaient Moriba Touré, sous-préfet de Womey, Dr Ibrahima Fernandez, directeur préfectoral de la Santé de N’Zérékoré, Dr Mamadou Aliou Barry, directeur général adjoint de l’hôpital régional, Pépé Kpogohomou, chef du centre de santé de Womey, et Moïse Mamy, pasteur évangélique. Le drame avait provoqué une vive émotion à N’Zérékoré et au-delà. Il avait également illustré les conséquences dramatiques de la peur et de la désinformation autour d’Ebola. Le CPJ avait alors souligné que des rumeurs accusant les agents de santé de propager le virus circulaient dans certaines communautés. Un procès, puis des condamnations L’affaire a été ensuite portée devant la justice. En avril 2015, le tribunal de premièreinstance de N’Zérékoré a condamné onze (11) personnes à la réclusion criminelle à perpétuité pour leur implication dans le meurtre collectif des huit membres de la mission. Human Rights Watch a toutefois relevé, dans son rapport de 2016, des préoccupations concernant l’absence d’enquête sur certaines exactions qui auraient été commises par des membres des forces de sécurité dans les suites du drame. Douze ans après, Womey demeure ainsi un épisode marquant de l’histoire récente de la Guinée forestière : celui d’une mission partie sensibiliser une population confrontée à la peur d’une épidémie et qui s’est transformée en tragédie.

items.title: BOST cuts fuel exports to Burkina Faso and Mali to protect local supply
items.description: Ghana’s state-owned fuel distributor BOST Energies has cut diesel and ‌gasoline exports to neighbouring Burkina Faso and Mali since August, prioritising domestic demand, Managing Director Afetsi Awoonor said on Wednesday. Conflict in Ukraine and the Middle East has tightened oil and gas supplies globally , ​driving fuel prices to record highs in some countries ahead of peak harvest ​and winter demand. The Reuters Power Up newsletter by columnist Ron Bousso provides everything you need to know about the global energy industry. Sign up here. Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger depend heavily on fuel imports ⁠from coastal neighbours including Ghana and Ivory Coast. The three Sahelian countries are ​ruled by military governments that seized power in coups and are battling Islamist insurgencies linked ​to al Qaeda and Islamic State. BOST managed to supply only half of the 80,000 metric tons of fuel Burkina Faso requested in July and August, Awoonor told Reuters on the sidelines of an ​energy conference in Bangkok. During the same period, BOST exported 10,000 tons of fuel to ​Mali, though the country had requested an extra 40,000 tons for August and September, he added. In Ghana, where fuel importer and distributor BOST holds a 30% market share, diesel consumption continues to grow as economic activity expands, Awoonor said. “Supply is available, but it’s at a high cost,” Awoonor said, adding that sharp increases in demand had strained supplies and complicated efforts ​to keep domestic fuel ​prices stable. Diesel accounts ⁠for two-thirds of BOST’s supplies. Ghana’s fuel prices rose earlier this year on global supply fears but have since eased, helped ​by a stronger currency and government intervention. Awoonor also said BOST plans to build a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) terminal in the industrial city of Tema by the fourth quarter next year and to start importing cooking gas. The company plans to build an LPG ⁠storage ​facility in Kumasi, Ghana’s second-largest city, to distribute the ​fuel, he said, adding that the plan was to build terminals at six locations in phases.

items.title: Google-Pakistan deal raises data privacy concerns
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Media watchdog Freedom Network has penned an open letter to Google and the government, seeking to know what sa­­feguards will ensure that the tech giant’s recent partnership with Pakistan strengthens the country’s digital economy without creating a backdoor for surveillance, censorship or unrestricted access to citizens’ personal information. The Islamabad-based watchdog welcomed the signing of memoranda of understanding and agreements be­­tween Google and the governm­e­­nt after the company opened its of­­fice in Pakistan to advance the country’s digital vision, but expres­sed ap­­prehensions that the tech company and the government had not made details of their agreements public. “A big question is what exactly has been agreed? Will the government or Google publish all MoUs, agreements, contracts or other arra­ngements signed between them? If some provisions must remain confidential, who decided that and under what law?” Freedom Network asked in its alert shared with the media through a press release. The media watchdog asked if there were any undisclosed commitments concerning access to user data, content, metadata or government databases. “Under what circumstances can Pakistani authorities request information about Google users? Will every request require a valid legal process and judicial oversight? Will Google reject requests that are overly broad, vague or inconsistent with fundamental rights?” Media watchdog seeks details of MoUs, agreements Freedom Network was explicit in asking if any protection or unambiguous safeguards against government access to journalists’ Gmail, Google Drive, photos, YouTube accounts, search-related information or other data that could reveal confidential sources were part of the agreements and MoUs. The watchdog asked Google to commit itself to not removing any content merely because a government agency asks, or that requests for blocking or removal shall be assessed under transparent legal standards and users shall receive notice and an opportunity to challenge decisions where legally possible. Freedom Network also worried about where Pakistani citizens’ data would be stored as the country is developing a national data-governance framework that urges data sovereignty, minimum disclosure and citizens’ right to know who has accessed their information. “Will Pakistani users’ data be stored in Pakistan, overseas, or both?” it asked Google. “There should not be informal or undocumented data-sharing arrangements between Google and the Pakistan government.” The press release quoted the media watchdog as asking the tech company: “Who independently will audit Google’s compliance with privacy and human-rights safeguards in Pakistan? The answer should not be simply the government.” Published in Dawn, September 17th, 2026

Some critical questions
items.description: TRUE to tradition, a ‘plan’ to ‘reset’ the country’s entire structure has come down like an epiphany from apparently ‘non-political’ quarters. The plan envisages creating multiple provinces and changing the country’s very tapestry — its geography, topography, demography, ethnic relations, resource distribution, power sharing, and broader political calculus. The situation raises critical questions. Why new provinces? The interior minister, who announced the plan , hasn’t held forth on the reasoning or offered an acceptable justification for adopting such an extreme and hazardous course. However, he has mentioned bad governance, population implosion, and systemic failures as some of the causes. Nor are there any official authoritative studies proposing a close nexus between good governance and smaller administrative structures. In fact, the global landscape reveals a mixed pattern. Some countries have fewer or territorially larger constituent units, and yet they are stable, functional, even enviable. Others have multiple small units/ provinces, but are perennially afflicted with broken, inept and even failed political systems. The factors that generally determine the performance and vitality of a state are the legitimacy and efficacy of its political system, the character and ability of its leadership, and the maturity and capacity of its institutions — not only to deliver better governance, but also to meet the continuing challenges thrown up by ever-changing societal and state imperatives. In revitalising the ‘failed’ political systems, we don’t know if the so-called plan contemplates these factors. Who is demanding them? Interestingly, most of these ideas have originated outside regular political processes, whether as One Unit, Basic Democracy, ‘Islamisation’, enlightened moderation, or hybrid governance. People have always been on the receiving end of new-fangled ideas and their pernicious consequences. The call for a structural ‘reset’, too, appears to have similar origins. So far, none of the governments — federal, provincial or even local — or the mainstream political leaderships have called for restructuring the provinces. However, there is near-consensus across the political spectrum on creating provinces in south Punjab, and KP’s Hazara belt. In fact, the Punjab and KP assemblies passed resolutions for these provinces, but they went nowhere. Instead of new units, the country needs softer options to heal societal wounds. Reorganising the state structures would be an extremely risky exercise. India’s Congress party had included the ‘linguistic’ provinces in its manifesto as early as 1917. Yet, after Partition, both prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru and home minister Vallabhbhai Patel were reluctant to reorganise the states, fearing balkanisation of the fledgling country. It was many months of intense political agitations across the country, expert studies, judicial commissions, and a much-mourned fast unto death by Telugu nationalist Potti Sriramulu that finally brought the government around. Still, the Reorganisation Act of 1955 was not passed to improve governance but to group various linguistic communities in their own separate states. In other words, distinctive ethno-cultural identities were recognised and restored, rather than brutally denied and suppressed as would have been the case if the states had been broken up in a manner that dispersed the historically located ethno-cultural communities — something that is being contemplated here. Is referendum feasible? Perhaps encouraged by the smooth passage of the controversial 26th and 27th constitutional amendments, and not expecting a large section of the political establishment to oppose the proposed move, some elements here had appeared confident of securing the required numbers to ensure restructuring. However, the JUI-F, ANP, PTI, and even the ruling party’s major coalition partner have dug in their heels. In fact, even the prime minister and his party seem reluctant to support the restructuring, though some government ministers are backing it, albeit without the cabinet’s approval. Likewise, the Sindh Assembly has also rejected the break-up of the province. As a result, other means are being sought — preferably, a referendum to execute the plan. But a referendum would not validate the wholesale reorganisation of the state. It lacks legitimacy and credibility. It cannot be used to circumvent or be a substitute for the mandatory constitutional amendment. People will not accept it because every military dictator has used it to legitimise their rule. Instead, a referendum will be seen as farcical and incite public anger, triggering a maelstrom of pushback. Will the ‘plan’ succeed? Any idea, policy, or law that is imposed on the people has miserably failed to achieve its objectives; in fact, it has often led to disasters. Steamrolling the restructuring of provinces — against the will of the people — will further aggravate identity-driven politics across a fragile multiethnic landscape. It may even ignite the tinderbox the country has become, particularly for poor and disgruntled youth who have endured the harrowing realities of failed systems. The numbers are dreadful. Half the population lives in poverty, around 28 million children are out of school, four out of 10 children suffer from stunted growth, three-fourths of the populace is consuming contaminated water, and the increasingly murky security environment scares away local and foreign investors. In these dire circumstances, the country desperately needs softer options to heal societal wounds — options that recompense the people through justice, equity, peace, opportunity, and development, which are democracy’s tested tools. The yawning fault lines — ethnic, social, political, inter-provincial and centre-province — must be mended, and federal democracy, which remains buried under the hybrid regime, restored. The system does need a ‘reset’. But the reset should mean building efficient and accountable institutions, strengthening rules-based governance, and allowing legitimate and representative leadership to run political and public offices. That requires a continuous process of fair, free elections held on time, so that dead wood can be replaced with a fresher, cleaner leadership at the federal, provincial, and local levels. Finally, a ‘reset’ would be fatal if it ignored the emotional, even spiritual, bonding of the various ethno-cultural communities with their respective provinces. This bonding goes beyond ideology or politics. It is the product of the centuries-long interplay between these communities and their distinctive land, history, culture, language, literature and art. This bonding leads many in Sindh to conceive their province as an indivisible historical entity — a firmer federalised version of Scotland or Quebec. The writer is a lawyer. shahabusto@hotmail.com Published in Dawn, September 17th, 2026

items.title: Ghana Gas to decide on $500 million gas pipeline early next year, CEO says
items.description: State-owned Ghana Gas plans to make a final investment decision by early next year on a long-discussed $500 million pipeline project that would transport gas from its processing plant in the western part of the country to industries in the southeast, CEO Judith Adjobah Blay said on Wednesday. The proposed 278-kilometre (173-mile) West-East onshore pipeline will enable the company to meet ⁠growing industrial sector demand and reduce its reliance on the West African pipeline shared ​by neighbouring countries, Blay told Reuters on the sidelines of the Gastech conference. “It’s a project ​that we hope to really embark on by the end of the first quarter of 2027,” she said, as the company is trying to line up financing. The project has been under discussion for nearly a decade as Ghana seeks cheaper, more reliable gas supplies to power industries in the Tema industrial enclave. Ghana Gas expects to receive more gas from the Eni-operated offshore Sankofa project when its ‌production increases ⁠to 350 million standard cubic feet per day (mmscfd) in 2028, Blay said, up from 280 mmscfd currently. The company processes about 130 mmscfd of associated gas from the Tullow-operated Jubilee and TEN oil fields, she said. The fields have an extra 50 mmscfd of gas available, which will be processed at a proposed gas processing plant that needs lawmaker approval before more details can be announced, Blay said. The plan would be for the government to take a 30% stake in the proposed plant, with the remainder funded by private firms, she added. Ghana’s gas consumption is forecast to reach 715 mmscfd by 2030, up from 502 mmscfd this year, according to the company. Ghana imports 70 mmscfd of lean gas from Nigeria, she said. “The ⁠policy ​is to use gas primarily for power production,” she ​said, as that would reduce the need to burn costlier fuels.

items.title: 2027: ‘Who is more Kwankwasiyya than us? We’ll deliver Kano for Tinubu’ — Jibrin
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye A member of the House of Representatives, Abdulmumin Jibrin, has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu will win Kano State in the 2027 presidential election, despite the political influence of former governor Rabiu Kwankwaso. Jibrin, who represents Kiru/Bebeji Federal Constituency of Kano State, stated this on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, while discussing the political situation in Kano ahead of the 2027 election. Kwankwaso, a former two-term governor of Kano, is the running mate to the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, in the 2027 election. Jibrin, who has previously been associated with the Kwankwasiyya political movement, said he and other APC politicians in Kano understood the movement and its political structure. He said, “Who is more Kwankwasiyya than us? We understand the entire dynamics, Seun, if you want me to put a bet, I will put a bet with you, we will deliver Kano for the President (Tinubu), and the president will win in the 2027 election.” The lawmaker said the political perception surrounding Tinubu’s support in Kano should not be mistaken for the actual electoral outcome, arguing that the result of the election would provide the clearest picture of voters’ choices. “Yes, there is always perception but I keep telling people that what will produce the real picture of what is on ground is the election results. Nigeria is a not a country that you could say you have a cooling system that could give you an idea of what the people are going through. Yes, there are challenges,” he said. Jibrin further claimed that Tinubu’s support had increased in northern Nigeria. “The president has never been liked so much as he is being liked in the Northern part of the country,” he said. On the APC’s preparations in Kano, Jibrin said the party’s political leaders were already working together ahead of the election. “In Kano, we are preparing ourselves, the governor is very much on ground and experienced. The deputy governor is extremely experienced, the deputy senate president is there. Senator Hanga is there, Kabiru Gaya is there, Shekarau is there, the chairman, appropriations committee is there (Bichi), we are meeting daily, we understand the dynamics,” he said. Jibrin’s comments come amid heightened political realignments ahead of the 2027 presidential election, with Obi and Kwankwaso now campaigning together on the NDC ticket, while Tinubu seeks a second term on the platform of the All Progressives Congress. The lawmaker had also previously expressed confidence that Tinubu would defeat Kwankwaso in Kano, while acknowledging that the former governor remained influential in the state and retained a significant support base. items.title: Dealers await answers as fuel subsidy rollout begins
items.description: • Petroleum dealers lament lack of clarity on payment mechanism, timeline • PM wants facilitation desks to help people trying to buy subsidised fuel • Ogra attributes hike to elevated crude prices despite decline in int’l rates ISLAMABAD: Even as members of the public who have signed up for the PM’s Fuel Relief Scheme queued up at fuel pumps late on Wednesday night, petroleum dealers were still not clear about the mechanism whereby they would be compensated. The concern was voiced by the Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association (PPDA) during a presser in Karachi, where its chairman Malik Khuda Bakhsh said that no fuel pump could afford to bear a loss of Rs100 per litre without clarity on how they will be compensated. He claimed that between the petroleum ministry, Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) and even the finance ministry, no one had been able to answer their questions. “Officials from Ogra and oil marketing companies say that the petroleum ministry will possibly pay the subsidy amount, whereas ministry officials maintain that payments will be made by the finance ministry, while finance ministry officials assure us that the State Bank will release the funds in a day or two,“ Mr Bakhsh added. A day earlier, the National Steering Com­mittee on Fuel Subsidy — chaired by Deputy PM Ishaq Dar — had ordered that payments to fuel stations under the PM’s scheme be processed within 24 hours through the State Bank of Pakistan. However, Mr Bakhsh said the federal government had assured dealers that they would be taken into confidence before the launch of the fuel relief package, but lamented that no such consultation took place. ”The government has to understand that if payments are not reimbursed in time, many dealers will stop participating in [the scheme], as many previous promises were also not fulfilled by the government,” he added. PPDA Vice Chairman Tariq Hassan said that around 14,000 dealers across the country have been trying desperately to contact the government over the past three days, adding that whenever Islamabad wants to enforce something, it stops communication. Another vice chairman, Anwar Kamal, said that if the scheme was to be successful, the government must negotiate with dealers, adding that dealers could not afford to have billions tied up for a long period under this scheme. Mr Bakhsh later told Dawn they had been invited to a virtual meeting with the relevant federal secretary on Thursday morning. He added that Ogra officials had also reached out to brief him, but he had asked for that information in writing, so he could relay that to the members of his association. Facilitation desks Earlier, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ordered authorities to set up facilitation desks comprising administration officials, volunteers and petrol pump staff to assist citizens in easily obtaining fuel subsidy under the special relief scheme, which was rolled out across the country at Wednesday midnight, following the launch of the pilot phase in Islamabad. Presiding over a meeting to review progress on the scheme, PM Shehbaz directed that personnel deployed at the facilitation desks should guide eligible citizens and provide them with all possible assistance in registration and other necessary procedures. The prime minister also asked the relevant authorities to remain proactive in creating public awareness about the scheme, which will benefit people from all four provinces, Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan. The meeting was informed that the scheme had been designed in a simple and easy-to-understand manner for the public. Only four pieces of information were required for registration: the applicant’s CNIC number, vehicle number plate, province of registration and vehicle registration date. Complete details of the fuel subsidy scheme are available in Urdu on www.pmfuelrelief.pk. According to an official, the number of successful registrations was gradually rising, while provincial governments were extending “full cooperation” for nationwide implementation of the scheme. Oil prices Meanwhile, notifying fresh POL rates on Wednesday night, Ogra attributed the steep hikes to elevated international crude oil and petroleum product prices. The price of high-speed diesel was increased by Rs5.62 per litre to Rs421.45, while petrol became costlier by Rs6.88 per litre, taking its new price to Rs391.22 per litre. However, Reuters reported on Wednesday night that oil prices fell in the open market on reports that Saudi Arabia was offering additional crude cargoes through Oman eased some concerns about Middle East supply disruptions. Brent crude futures fell $2.92, or 2.7 per cent, to settle at $105.83 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate futures fell $3.40, or 3.2pc, to close at $102.43, Reuters reported. Saudi Arabia is offering more loadings of crude oil to Asian refiners via ship-to-ship transfers off Oman’s Sohar port, people familiar with the matter said, blunting some of the hit to global supply from attacks on the country’s East-West pipeline to the Red Sea. Oil prices had gained more than $3 in the previous session after shipping industry sources said crude loadings at Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea export hub of Yanbu had been suspended and Riyadh had cancelled some cargo deliveries to European customers. The suspension followed strikes on the East-West pipeline, which feeds the Saudi port of Yanbu. It became the main Saudi outlet for oil exports after Iran began blockading the Strait of Hormuz after US and Israeli attacks on the country. Published in Dawn, September 17th, 2026
